exposure: level of spinal cord injury (e.g., below T5, above T5)
cohort: The study included 10 patients with spinal cord injury who had 17 analyzable pregnancies (including one twin pregnancy) between 2003 and 2014.
finding: The study found a high rate of prematurity and cesarean section in pregnant patients with spinal cord injury, but observed good maternal and perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was possible in lesions below T5, while higher lesions (above T5) necessitated scheduled cesarean sections; the study reported 58.82% cesarean sections and 41.18% vaginal deliveries.
